subtitle: Someone has borrowed tomorrow's tide.
briefing: Rescue pilot Edda from the blocked estuary. Capture both sounding outworks and escort her to the fishing village, where she can show the townspeople why their boats are stranded.
debrief: The outworks held a forged sluice order. Edda's soundings show water diverted into an abandoned quarry, exposing the wreck of a debt ship. The salvage factor is making workers recover its ledgers before anyone can compare the books.
hints: Merfolk can cross deep water and move normally on plains. Forests, groves and hills slow them and increase incoming damage.
Shallows are neutral for merfolk; swamps protect them. Land troops are exposed in both.
Keep Edda alive. Shore guards can reach Mira across the sandbars; protect the approaches while swimmers flank the outworks through deep water.

legacyDialogue.speaker: Captain Vale
legacyDialogue.text: The factor pays us to keep this channel clear for salvage. Bring your accusation to the council; you will not cross my posts.

intro.speaker: Mira
intro.text: The tide should have returned by dawn. Our nets are dry; their boats are on the mud. This is no quarrel either shore can afford.

intro.speaker: Edda
intro.text: Vale's men took the sounding posts. I saw a sluice order bearing the council seal, but the date was cut from an older sheet.

intro.speaker: Postmaster Harl
intro.text: Captain Vale sent us to hold these posts for the factor's salvage crew. Bring your accusation to the council; you will not cross here.

intro.speaker: Mira
intro.text: Then we take the posts and bring the pilot. Leave the fishing houses standing.

victory.speaker: Edda
victory.text: Here are my soundings, and his order. The quarry gate is open. The water did not disappear; someone moved it.

victory.speaker: Mira
victory.text: We cannot just close that gate. There are workers inside the wreck, below the next high tide.
